items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 2 Dec (UK only). Ahead of the London run of Hamlet Hail to the Thief at the Barbican Theatre, Mary Anne Hobbs joins Thom Yorke alongside directors and Co-Creators Steven Hoggett and Christine Jones, actors Samuel Blenkin who plays Hamlet, Ami Tredrea who plays Ophelia, and arranger Justin Levine at rehearsals for their acclaimed collaboration that brings together Shakespeare's Hamlet and Radiohead's landmark 2003 album Hail to the Thief. items.title: Thom Yorke, Christine Jones and Steven Hoggett, Hamlet Hail to the Thief

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 25 Nov (UK only). One Leg One Eye is the project of Ian Lynch (founding member of Irish group Lankum) and George Brennan, exploring submerged leylines of music and song, drawing on the raw aesthetics of black metal, noise, and drone, while also being deeply imbued with a sense of history and myth. George selects a track for our End of Days library to pass on to future generations. And on the anniversary of Back To Black we hear from Maggi Hambling, one of the UK’s most iconic Artists, about painting Amy Winehouse as a wall of water. Produced by BBC Audio for BBC Radio 6 Mu…
items.title: One Leg One Eye + Maggi Hambling

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 18 Nov (UK only). Henry Rollins talks about his lifelong love of The Cramps and the discovery of Gravest Gravy, a previously unheard album recorded by the band in 1977. The long-lost tapes were found in Poison Ivy's garage and Rollins and Ian MacKaye, helped restore the recordings and prepare them for release. With renewed interest in the band Rollins also discusses plans for future archival releases as more of The Cramps' legacy. Produced by BBC Audio for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: Henry Rollins on The Cramps

items.desc: On BBC Sounds until 11 Nov (UK only). Norwegian Mexican artist and DJ Carmen Villain provides an ambient mix for Slow Sunday. Her new album Memoria is out now via Smalltown Supersound. Marina Herlop, the Catalan pianist and composer, selects her choice for our End of Days music library to pass on to future generations. Produced by BBC Audio for BBC Radio 6 Music.
items.title: Slow Sunday: With an ambient guest mix from Carmen Villain

items.desc: Natural history filmmaker Kathryn Jeffs has worked on acclaimed series Planet Earth, Frozen Planet and Monsoon. Her latest project is Earth's Tropical Islands which will be broadcast on New Years Day on BBC 2. The series journeys to three of the most mysterious and remote islands on planet earth: Madagascar, Borneo and Hawaii and will reveal how these isolated and iconic tropical islands harbour remarkable wildlife and human castaways found nowhere else on Earth. items.title: With Kathryn Jeffs
